alkylation reagent: and then alkylated with methyl methanethiosulfonate (10 mM).
alkylation concentration: and then alkylated with methyl methanethiosulfonate (10 mM).
cleavage agent: subjected to protein digestion with sequencing grade modified trypsin (Promega, Madison, WI) at 37°C.
collision energy: For HCD, normalized collision energy was set to 28.
enrichment method: Mitochondria were magnetically enriched by labeling with 50 μl of anti-TOM22 MicroBeads in separation buffer for 1 h at 4°C.
fractionation method: Then iTRAQ-labeled peptides were desalted using Sep-Pak C18 cartridges, vacuum dried and fractionated on a C18 column (4.6 × 200 mm, 5 μm, 300 Å) (PolyLC, Columbia, MD, USA) at a flow rate of 1.0 ml/min using HPLC.
fragmentation method: The 10 most intense ions above a 1000 count threshold were selected for HCD fragmentation
instrument: The LC-MS/MS analysis was performed using the Dionex Ultimate 3000 RSLC nanoLC system coupled to a Q-Exactive apparatus (Thermo Fisher, MA).
ionization type: Peptides were analyzed on a Dionex EASY-spray column (PepMap® C18, 3um, 100A) using an EASY nanospray source at an electrospray potential of 1.5 kV.
labeling: this study adopted a discovery-driven approach with isobaric tag for relative and absolute quantitation (iTRAQ) and label-free quantitative proteomics
reduction reagent: The gel pieces were reduced with Tris 2- carboxyethyl phosphine hydrochloride (5 mM)
reduction concentration: The gel pieces were reduced with Tris 2- carboxyethyl phosphine hydrochloride (5 mM)
